channel.title: Vision For Xperiences — News
channel.description: VFX, 3D animation, live visuals, interactive installations and drone work, from the Vision For Xperiences studio desk.

item.title: WebGPU just went baseline across every browser
item.description: Native-class 3D performance in the browser is no longer a future idea. Studios building browser-based work need to think differently about target platforms.

item.title: 3D printing moves from novelty to production tooling for live work
item.description: As additive manufacturing proves itself on commercial sets and in prop houses, the time to bake it into job estimates is now.

item.title: Does one studio really handle previz through delivery
item.description: Some do, but the trend is toward specialists who know when to hand off. Here's how to tell the difference.

item.title: Houdini 22 brings MCP agents into character rigging workflows
item.description: SideFX wired AI code generation into KineFX, letting riggers scaffold procedural setups faster without surrendering control.

item.title: DJI Avata 360 shifts FPV from linear chase work to 360 capture
item.description: Eight-kilohertz 360-degree video and single-lens fallback mode open new options for spatial storytelling and post-production freedom.

item.title: ISO 22028-5 sets a common language for HDR still image colour
item.description: A new international standard published in May defines how studios encode, store, and deliver HDR photographs and graphics with consistent colour across devices.

item.title: Vicon acquires face capture firm, closing the pipeline gap
item.description: Facial and body performance capture have always come from different vendors. That just changed.

item.title: Open source flips the commercial 3D software economics
item.description: Vendor lock-in is now the top reason organizations choose free tools over licensed subscriptions, reshaping how studios pitch to clients and how they budget.

item.title: How to pick a studio for a 3D product animation
item.description: Current rates span from 5k to 25k per finished minute. We mapped who does what work and at what price point.

item.title: Building real-time interactive experiences for museums and exhibitions
item.description: A practical guide to finding the right studio for hands-on installations that respond to visitors in real time.

item.title: August broke open the Gaussian splatting toolkit
item.description: Major VFX and 3D software shipped native splat support in five days, signalling production is no longer an experiment.
